Corydoras desana Lima & Sazima, 2017. Common names: CW011, Orca Cory, Kopansermalle (Denmark).

Identification: Corydoras are identified by their twin rows of armour plates along the flanks and by having fewer than 10 dorsal fin rays. They are most commonly confused with the other genera in the sub-family, namely Brochis, Scleromystax and Aspidoras.

IUCN Red List: Data Deficient (last assessed 2020).

Known only from upriver in the Igarapé Castanha, a tributary of the rio Tiquié (Amazon, Middle Amazon (Solimões), Negro, Upper Negro, Uaupés, Tiquié). Type locality: Igarapé Castanha, tributary of rio Tiquié, village of Santa Rosa, São Gabriel da Cachoeira, Amazonas, Brazil.

Ideally the substrate should be sand, but rounded gravel is an imperfect alternative. Avoid rough-edged (chipped) gravel, which increases the risk of damage to the fish's barbels when it digs. Border the substrate with driftwood and aquatic plants, leaving an open area for foraging and swimming. Shade from overhanging rockwork, arching bogwood, and tall or floating plants is all that is required to settle these fish.

Will readily accept all prepared foods that reach the bottom of the aquarium such as tablets, granules and larger flakes. Live or frozen foods such as bloodworm, white worm, grindal worm (Enchytraeus), Daphnia and Tubifex are readily accepted and good for conditioning groups of fish for spawning.
Females grow larger and are more full-bodied, best observed from above. Males typically have more pointed rather than rounded fin tips as they mature.
